free_tier.stated: Port forwarding is only included on Windscribe's paid plans. The free plan carries 2 GB per month, or 10 GB per month with a confirmed email, and reaches servers in 10 countries, not all locations. Pro: $9/month or $69/year ($5.75/month).

egress.terms: Users get unlimited bandwidth to use and can connect to all 69+ countries. This also provides access to all features including the fully customizable R.O.B.E.R.T., port forwarding, as well as custom configs for all locations.; ingress: tcp+udp

interface_detail: Dashboard request for a port; configs downloaded from the account. Protocols: WireGuard, OpenVPN (UDP or TCP), IKEv2, Stealth and WStunnel. Obfuscation: Stealth and WStunnel, plus a Circumvent Censorship option. Hosted SOCKS5 servers were discontinued; desktop apps host a local SOCKS5 or HTTP proxy through Proxy Gateway. P2P is allowed except on locations marked with a crossed-out P2P label.
tooling: Official app and account dashboard; WireGuard custom configs on Pro.
chaining: Useful as a short-lived test endpoint for a free VM; not a fixed address without the static IP add-on.

limits.value: ephemeral port lasts 7 days: The Windscribe Pro Plan includes support for ephemeral port forwarding, which lasts for 7 days at a time. All users requesting ephemeral port forwarding configurations will be granted one for 1 week before being cleared out.
a permanent port requires a separately charged static IP: If you prefer a permanent port, you can get one with a static IP charged separately to a Pro subscription.

binding_note: Volume does not bind because Pro is unlimited. What fails first is the 7-day reclaim: the port is explicitly cleared and reissued, so a long-running service loses its address weekly unless a static IP is bought on top of Pro.

identity_cost.detail: An account for any persistent configuration; the free tier is reachable without payment and the site advertises No credit card, no logs, no catch.

reliability_note: Port reclaimed every 7 days by design; a client that does not re-request loses ingress with no error at the service.
confidence_note: Measured would need a Pro account and a byte count. The 7-day reclaim sentence is the vendor's own FAQ answer, read.

evidence.proved: Port forwarding is Pro only, ephemeral ports last 7 days, a permanent port needs a static IP add-on, and free plans get no forwarding.
Pro is $9 per month or $69 per year and includes port forwarding; the free plan carries 2 to 10 GB per month.
The free tier exists with no card and 10 global locations, which is why the paid tier is the one that forwards.

evidence.quote: Pro can be purchased for $9/month on a monthly basis or $69/year ($5.75/month) on a yearly plan.

evidence.proved: Windscribe offers six protocols incl. OpenVPN over UDP and TCP

evidence.quote: This protocol is very similar to Stealth but has its own nuances.

evidence.quote: Applies protocol-level adjustments for [WireGuard®](https://windscribe.com/features/flexible-connectivity/), OpenVPN, and Stealth

evidence.proved: Free reaches 10 countries and is capped at 10 GB per month with a confirmed email
evidence.quote: Free users can access servers in 10 different countries and with a confirmed email address, with data usage capped at 10GB/month.

evidence.proved: Free is 10 country servers with no card required
evidence.quote: Either way, it's 10 country servers, unlimited devices on one account, and no card unless you want to.

price_per_tb_month: USD 9 per month; USD 69 per year; static IP charged separately
notes: The static IP is the real product for ingress here, and its price is on a separate page that did not read, so the cheapest stable-port figure for Windscribe is unknown rather than zero. A 7-day port is enough for a demo and not enough for a service with a DNS record.

extras.wg_detail: Custom configurations are a Pro feature per the pricing article: access to all features including the fully customizable R.O.B.E.R.T., port forwarding, as well as custom configs for all locations. The port itself is requested from the account dashboard.
